summary: The brainstorm's verified-codebase section survives a 13-day drift check almost intact: every load-bearing mechanism it anchors the design to (open crew/stream routes, tenant-from-body with 'global' defaults, PBAC fail-open, the two AgentsFlow result-fidelity fix sites, usage-record PII stripping, the LLMFactory api_key injection point, the Pulumi executor gaps, navrules' zero consumers, ArtifactStore's tenant-less keying, documentdb as crew-result default) re-verifies today, though most line anchors moved. One design element is now contradicted by a recorded repo decision: FEAT-421 rejected app.py-middleware tenancy for formdesigner (per-route decorator + tenant-in-URL instead), so the brainstorm's tenant_middleware needs an explicit architectural answer rather than silent adoption. Three new facts sharpen the plan: a fourth ContextVar-capture site exists in clients/base.py, FlowDefinition models are now closed (extra=forbid) with a live stored-definition-compatibility concern, and definition.py already declares an unwired enable_execution_memory knob that S3b should consume.

constraints.statement: A recorded repo decision (FEAT-421, decision memory on PRs #1146/#1149, TASK-2205) rejects aiohttp middleware in app.py as the tenancy enforcement point and establishes per-route decorators + URL-declared tenant as the shipped pattern.
FlowDefinition models are closed (extra=forbid) and already-stored definitions must stay loadable; adding tenant/new fields requires a compatibility story for stored bundles.
Tenant/run ContextVars must be captured at event construction in all FOUR clients/base.py sites (a fourth appeared after the FEAT-438 client rebase).
Policy guards are no longer fully dormant: dataset_manager sources consume DataPlanePolicyGuard/RlsPredicate at runtime, so S0's fail-closed work must not break that consumer.

The unauthenticated crew surface grew since the brainstorm (tales-research POST handler, durable job progress), so S0's route inventory must be re-enumerated at spec time rather than copied from the brainstorm.

hypotheses.statement: Option C (core tenancy primitives + ai-parrot-saas satellite control plane) remains the right architecture, and the brainstorm's phased plan (S0 first, S3a in parallel) survives verification unchanged. The design needs exactly one amendment: the tenant-boundary enforcement mechanism (S1) must be reconciled with the FEAT-421 decorator precedent — either justify why a middleware is structurally sound for a SaaS-owned subapp (own app assembly, M2M API-key paths with no navigator session) or adopt a decorator/subapp-scoped variant.

claims.statement: S0's predicate holds: the three crew handler files carry no @is_authenticated and tenant comes from query/body with 'global' defaults on reads.
Stream routes still self-exclude from navigator-auth (stream.py:385-394).
setup_pbac fails open by design and PARROT_SAAS_MODE does not exist yet.

S3a's two fix sites re-verify at flow.py:1881 and flow.py:988; build_node_metadata's generic branch drops usage entirely; the checkpoint-resume path already passes response=, proving the intended call shape.
AgentsFlow has zero ExecutionMemory wiring, but definition.py:328 already declares an unwired enable_execution_memory knob S3b should consume.
FlowDefinition still lacks a tenant field, and the models are now closed with a stored-definition compatibility concern on record.
UsageRecord remains PII-free with no tenant dimension and in-process cumulative cost; capture-at-construction now spans four sites in clients/base.py.
Per-run BYOK key injection via LLMFactory.create(api_key=...) works today (factory.py:273) and is unused.
PulumiToolkit still discards config_values ('not yet implemented' in its own docstrings) and never honors state_backend or runs pulumi login.
navrules still has zero consumers outside its own package.
CREW_RESULT_STORAGE defaults to documentdb and ArtifactStore has no tenant dimension — both open questions from the brainstorm remain live and unanswered by code.
The brainstorm's §1 middleware design conflicts with the reasoning of a recorded decision (FEAT-421); the conflict is about mechanism, not about the tenancy model itself.
No competing or overlapping SaaS/tenancy/metering work has started in sdd/ since the brainstorm.

unknowns.question: S1 enforcement mechanism: does the SaaS surface use an aiohttp middleware (as the brainstorm designs) or the FEAT-421 per-route decorator pattern? The recorded objections (wheel doesn't ship app.py; root-router mounting) may not apply to a SaaS-owned subapp with its own app factory, but adopting middleware without addressing that decision on paper invites a justified revert.
unknowns.user_answer: FEAT-421 decorator pattern: generalize requires_tenant() — per-route decorator with the tenant declared in the URL (/api/v1/saas/t/{tenant}/...), no middleware anywhere. The decorator must also cover the M2M API-key path (resolve principal from the bearer key when no navigator session exists), fail-closed. Amends brainstorm §1.

unknowns.question: When `tenant` (and the enable_execution_memory wiring) is added to the closed FlowDefinition models, what is the compatibility policy for already-stored definitions and future catalog bundles — silent default injection on load, a schema_version bump on the definition, or a one-time migration?
unknowns.user_answer: Optional fields + safe defaults — already-stored definitions load unchanged, no schema_version bump; extra=forbid only rejects unknown input fields, which new optional fields don't violate.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and freshly re-verified; the program is already decomposed into 14+ specs by the brainstorm itself, so the next artifact is the first spec, not another exploration round. S0 blocks everything sellable; S3a is independent, two call sites plus a helper, and unblocks dossier and billing fidelity.
